programme: ATRX loss marks the MSI-prone, immunologically active molecular subtype of endometrial carcinoma; EOMES drives the canonical cytotoxic CD8+ effector program (its own targets here are IFNG, CD8A, PRF1, IL2, IL2RB, NOTCH1 — textbook effector-CTL genes), and under sustained antigen exposure that effector program converts into a TOX-dependent exhausted state, with TOX flagged in the record as a pan-cancer immune-checkpoint/exhaustion factor.
role_in_a: None of the three carries independent, disease-specific support in fibromyalgia here: no Open Targets association for ATRX, TOX, or EOMES, and the only retrieved papers touching TOX/EOMES under the fibromyalgia query are about ME/CFS, not fibromyalgia. At best this programme is 'expected' by analogy to general chronic-immune-dysregulation hypotheses in fibromyalgia-adjacent conditions, not documented for fibromyalgia itself in this material.
role_in_b: Documented at the level of endometrial cancer's known molecular subtyping: ATRX mutation is associated with the MSI-prone, immunologically active endometrial tumor subgroup (PMID 36247274); TOX carries a high Open Targets score in this disease (percentile 0.9166) and is proposed as a pan-cancer immune-checkpoint/exhaustion factor with single-cell evidence for driving T-cell exhaustion (PMID 32111241, 39152366). EOMES itself has no UCEC-specific placement in the record, but its target profile is the effector program that precedes TOX-driven exhaustion.
shared_axis: There is no documented or anatomically obvious reason a centralized chronic pain disorder would share a tumor-infiltrating-lymphocyte exhaustion axis with an immunologically active endometrial cancer subtype; the only bridge available is a generic 'chronic T-cell dysregulation' argument, not a specific mechanism tying these two diseases together.
reasoning: ATRX and TOX are independently, and fairly strongly, placed in UCEC by Open Targets score plus on-topic titles, and EOMES's target list is textbook effector-CTL biology, so the module is real and nameable; but the UCEC evidence is pancancer/data-mining rather than UCEC-specific mechanism, EOMES itself is unplaced, and the fibromyalgia side has zero retrieved evidence, so the cross-disease claim rests on reasoning, not retrieval.
support: PMID 36247274 — ties ATRX mutation to immunologically active, MSI-prone endometrial-cancer-relevant tumor characteristics. PMID 39152366 — pancancer analysis proposing TOX as a candidate immune checkpoint across cancers, UCEC included only by extension. PMID 32111241 — single-cell evidence that TOX drives T-cell exhaustion, the general mechanism invoked here, not shown specifically in UCEC tissue. PMID 33490273, 40775769, 39073402 — pancancer/data-mining analyses that include UCEC as one dataset among many but add no UCEC-specific mechanistic detail.
how_to_falsify: Stratify UCEC TCGA (or a fresh cohort) by ATRX mutation status and test by single-cell RNA-seq or multiplex IHC whether TOX+EOMES co-expression marks exhausted CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes specifically in the ATRX-mutant/MSI-high tumors; no enrichment would break the UCEC half. Separately, assay PBMCs or muscle-infiltrating lymphocytes from fibromyalgia patients for TOX/EOMES expression or an exhaustion phenotype; absence would remove the fibromyalgia half entirely.
caveats: Blood (fibromyalgia) versus uterine tissue (UCEC) is a distant tissue pairing with no known comorbidity, and the concordance fractions rest on 24 patient-group comparisons from a single independent cohort pair. ATRX, TOX, and EOMES sit in the lower-to-middle half of the recurrence range (24/24 down to 12/24), well below the two most robust factors in this pair, ZNF219 (24/24) and TCF20 (23/24), which carry no interpretable biology or literature here and were excluded from this account for that reason — a story built on the top-ranked factors would look different. TCF7, a canonical TOX/EOMES partner in exhaustion/stemness biology, was removed as tissue-generic, so its absence here reflects the exclusion filter, not counter-evidence. PPARGC1A, PHB1, KLF14, ZIC2, HOXB4, and COPS5 literature was explicitly flagged as unconfirmed or off-target and was not used to build this account.
